trick: Read pH as a distance from 7. Below 7 acidic, above 7 basic, and each step is ten times, not one step. So pH 3 is not a little more acidic than pH 5, it is a hundred times more.

video.query: acids bases salts pH scale indicators neutralisation class 9 chemistry

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about acids, bases and salts.

items.statement: An acid turns blue litmus red.
items.why: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. Litmus is the one indicator that works both ways.

items.statement: A pH of 7 means the solution is strongly basic.
items.why: A pH of 7 is neutral, which is pure water. Basic solutions lie above 7.

items.statement: An acid reacting with a base gives a salt and water.
items.why: This is neutralisation, and it is why an antacid settles an upset stomach.

items.statement: Acid should be poured into water, never water into acid.
items.why: Dilution releases a great deal of heat. Adding acid slowly to water lets the water absorb it; the other way round can boil and spit acid out.
Only the bases that dissolve in water are called alkalis. Copper oxide is a base but not an alkali.

trick: Work needs movement in the direction of the force. Hold a heavy bag still for an hour and you have done no work at all in physics, however tired you are. And power is not how much work but how fast, so the same work done in half the time is double the power.

video.query: work energy and power formula numericals class 9 physics

data.prompt: Choose the right relation for each quantity, and see why the others do not fit.

items.ask: Work done by a constant force along the direction of motion
items.why: Work is force multiplied by the distance moved in the direction of the force. Time does not enter it at all, which is why holding something still does no work.
Power is the rate of doing work, so work divided by time. Multiplying by time would make a slow worker the more powerful one.

items.ask: Kinetic energy of a moving body
items.why: Kinetic energy depends on the square of the speed, so doubling the speed gives four times the energy. m g h is potential energy, which depends on height instead.
Force is mass times acceleration, not mass times velocity. Mass times velocity is momentum, a different quantity with different units.

trick: Sound needs a material to travel through, so there is no sound in a vacuum. And one relation carries every numerical: speed equals frequency times wavelength. Write v = f λ at the top of the page before you read the question.

data.problem: A tuning fork of frequency 500 Hz makes a sound that travels through air at 340 metres per second. Find the wavelength.

steps.ask: Which relation connects speed, frequency and wavelength?
steps.why: Speed equals frequency times wavelength. Check it with units: hertz is per second, metres times per second gives metres per second.

steps.why: Divide both sides by the frequency.
340 divided by 500 is 0.68 metres, that is 68 centimetres. The third option is what you get by multiplying instead of dividing.
